title: AP Exclusive: Maine ICE Shooter Had Violent History, Mental Illness; Passed Vetting Anyway
excerpt: The Associated Press revealed that ICE officer David Brouillette, who fatally shot a Colombian man in Biddeford, Maine, had a documented history of mental health crises and domestic violence allegations — yet cleared ICE's background check during the agency's rapid hiring surge.
content:
On July 13, 2026, ICE officer David Brouillette fatally shot 25-year-old Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero during a vehicle stop in Biddeford, Maine. Four days later, the Associated Press published an exclusive report revealing that Brouillette had struggled with serious mental health issues since childhood and had been accused by two former spouses of violent and threatening behavior.

  • Family members told AP that Brouillette was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and ADHD as a child, was initially rejected by the military due to his diagnoses, and later experienced PTSD after military service.
  • One ex-wife alleged he had choked her, slammed her to the floor, and left a voicemail saying she and others "should have [their] throats cut." A second ex-wife filed a court document alleging he once threatened to kill her with a gun.
  • A judge had previously ordered Brouillette to temporarily relinquish his firearms, according to family court records cited by AP.
  • Despite these red flags — many allegedly discoverable in a standard background check — Brouillette was hired by ICE during its mass hiring surge under the Trump administration.

Border Czar Tom Homan acknowledged on CNN that if the allegations were true, Brouillette "would have had an almost impossible time to pass vetting" and "should not have ever cleared vetting." Homan announced that both the vetting process and training protocols were "under review."

Sen. Bennie Thompson stated the case "directly call[ed] into question the supposed vetting and training ICE does of its recruits," while Sen. Alex Padilla accused the administration of deploying "untrained, improperly vetted, or inexperienced" agents into communities.
